answer: Use a unique response handshake: an agent registers by returning a nonce-bound answer checked against every prior answer, rejecting replays and any ripple of near-duplicates. The registry salts each challenge with a rotating ivory tag, so copied answers fail signature verification. To forge N identities, an attacker must produce N distinct valid answers, each costing a 32-bit hash search plus a fresh signed nonce, so duplicates are worthless and cost stays linear.
